newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa confirms mine death toll as 20.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa confirms mine death toll as 20.

text.p: The death toll in a South African mining disaster was confirmed as 20 on Tuesday, with mine management saying that two miners initially feared killed were not on duty.
But in a new blow for the 200 surviving workers, the Roberts Victor Diamond Mine warned they could lose their jobs. The mine is owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc.
"The newest concern for the 200 surviving miners is whether the mine will be able to operate again and to provide them with employment," the mine-owners said in a statement.
"The owners and mine management intend to bring the mine back into production but the timing and cost must still be assessed," the statement said, without elaborating further.
The mine at Dealesville, some 60 km (38 miles) west of the Free State provincial capital Bloemfontein, was hit by an underground mudslide last week followed heavy rains.
Rescue teams abandoned their search for bodies last Thursday after it became too dangerous to continue, because mud was still flowing into the mine.
Twenty-two miners were feared dead but Rovic said one had been found to be off sick on the day and a second was believed to be absent without leave in Mozambique.
The dead were from South Africa, Lesotho and Mozambique. Some of their relatives were still being traced by the mine.
Seventeen people died in 1994 when a wall burst at a slimes dam at a gold mine at Virginia, also in the Free State province.
